A1.justification: Despite the changed title and organization, both PDFs describe the same OmniDFA framework and OmniFake dataset. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are sufficiently readable for a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attribution and detection experiments in Tables 2-4, plus robustness tests and component ablations in Figures 4-5.

after.justification: v2 reports original attribution and detection experiments, support-shot sensitivity results, component ablations, and degradation analyses, including Appendix F.

M1.justification: The dual-branch feature extractor, supervised contrastive and sphere-center losses, prototypical attribution, and Tukey-fence boundary update are retained. Appendix D expands the boundary calculation without establishing a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate OmniFake, GenImage, and Chameleon. OmniFake retains the same 45 generators and ten real-image sources. Detection, unseen-generator attribution, JPEG compression, and Gaussian-blur scenarios remain covered; the support-count change does not introduce a new task or population.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds POSE and OOC-CLIP to the attribution comparison while retaining the previous six comparators. UniversalAttr is shortened to UnivAttr. Comparator membership in the detection tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The primary attribution evaluation changes throughout from 5-way/15-way 5-shot to 5-way/15-way 10-shot. v2 also adds attribution Macro-F1 and Chameleon F1, materially revising the main evaluation protocol. Dataset folds, training configurations, and existing detection settings are retained.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Figure 4a add support-shot sensitivity from 1 to 200 samples for OmniDFA and FSD under both attribution tasks. Component ablations remain. The original class-specific degradation curves move from v1 Figure 4 to v2 Appendix F/Figure 6, with aggregate accuracy views added in Figure 4b.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 test episodes per attribution configuration and three-fold evaluation, without confidence intervals, significance tests, or training-seed variability. Table 10 restates the existing episode count rather than documenting additional repetitions.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the main attribution results and adds Macro-F1 and two comparator rows. OmniDFA's mean 5-way/15-way accuracies are 72.86%/50.24% at 5-shot in v1 and 75.34%/53.54% at 10-shot in v2; these are different-condition results, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Support-shot curves and Chameleon F1 results are added. Table 3 and the existing Table 4 accuracy values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds a formal support-set definition for N-way K-shot attribution. Appendix D explicitly defines quartile indexing and assumes the real-image batch size is divisible by four. The existing losses and Tukey/EMA boundary rule remain mathematically equivalent; no new theorem or proof is supplied.

C1.justification: Both versions claim a new few-shot paradigm for identifying unseen generators, the OmniFake dataset, and a unified framework with strong attribution and state-of-the-art detection generalization. The attribution-focused title and baseline framing change emphasis without materially changing these scientific contributions.

C2.justification: v2 interprets 10-shot evaluation as a performance-cost compromise and adds an explanation for angular rather than cosine boundary calculations. Its robustness discussion distinguishes JPEG resilience beyond training augmentation from deterioration under stronger blur, refining v1's broader beyond-range degradation statement.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising future code/data release to reporting availability at a repository. Table 10 newly discloses N-query = 5, Appendix D details boundary computation, and Table 9 clarifies bfloat16 precision. Most implementation settings and hardware disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: POSE is newly cited, while references including CIFAKE, AEROBLADE, and Stay-positive are removed. DE-FAKE is added to the dataset comparison table. Most related-work discussion already existed in v1 Appendix B and is moved, with limited revisions, to v2 Section 2.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially rewritten around few-shot attribution. Related work moves into the main paper, method subsections are reorganized around task formulation and a unified objective, and boundary explanations expand into a dedicated appendix. These constitute extensive narrative and structural revision.

P2.justification: v2 changes the page design, revises the task and architecture diagrams, expands Tables 1, 2, and 4, and adds Table 10. Figure 4 combines new sensitivity plots with aggregate robustness views, while the original robustness plots become appendix Figure 6. Table density, legends, axes, and placement also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly strengthens empirical support through additional attribution comparators, support-shot sensitivity, and F1 reporting, while improving evaluation and boundary documentation. The core method and detection evidence remain stable. Higher attribution scores use twice as many support samples and do not establish same-setting improvement; the denser tables also reduce readability. Overall, the added evidence and clearer specification provide a limited net quality gain.
